subject: Whether the release qualification live gate depends on Logic's UI language
question: Does the set of operations that fail their independent readback change when Logic's UI language changes?

host.note: measured in both ja-JP and en-US on the same machine and the same release binary; `host.locale` names the run that FAILED

reverify.command: Manual because no single command does it: (1) `defaults write com.apple.logic10 AppleLanguages -array ja` and relaunch Logic on a disposable project; (2) `swift build -c release`; (3) `swift test --no-parallel --filter realReleaseBinaryExecutesEveryOperationWithIndependentReadback`; (4) repeat (1)-(3) with `-array en`. The test lives in Tests/LogicProMCPTests/QualificationRunnerTests.swift and prints the live-gate lines this record quotes.
reverify.expected: ja-JP: failed=2 and the test fails on knownLiveGateFailuresMatchExactly; en-US: failed=1 and it passes
reverify.cost: ~25 s per run plus a Logic relaunch between them, so about five minutes in total

method: The same release binary driven twice by the same test, with nothing changed between the runs but Logic's UI language and the relaunch that requires.

observations.what: the live gate, by UI language

conclusion: The qualification live gate is not language-independent. `plugins.get_inventory` fails its own independent readback on a Japanese Logic and passes on an English one, with the same binary minutes apart — so the known-failure set the test compares against describes an English Logic, and running the suite on a Japanese one reports a failure that is about the environment. It is a further read the Japanese-labels issue reaches, and unlike the ones fixed alongside this record it is NOT fixed: nothing here says which of the response or the readback moved.
limits: It does not say WHY `plugins.get_inventory` disagrees with its readback in Japanese. No ja-JP probe of that operation was taken; only the gate's own verdict for it.
One host, one build, one project. `tracks.list_library` fails in both languages and is already pinned as a known failure against #284 — this record is about the operation that appears only in one.
The test is skipped entirely without a release build (`.enabled(if: isExecutableFile)`), which is why CI does not see this. It is a local-suite property, not a CI one.

`swift test` was run once per language, not repeatedly. A single run cannot separate a language dependence from a flake, though the two runs differ in exactly the direction the language change predicts.
